title: Typing useState: let it infer, or name a union

slides.say: Most of the time, use state needs no type at all. TypeScript reads it from the initial value.
Start with false, and the state is a boolean. Setting it to a string is an error.
Be explicit when the initial value is too narrow a hint. Here, a union of allowed strings. Without it, TypeScript would just infer string.
Even better, group related values into one union of objects. Data only exists on success, and error only on error.
